newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia money market rate rises to 9.6 vs 8.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia money market rate rises to 9.6 vs 8.7 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate rose to 9.6 percent on Wednesday from 8.7 percent, lifted by stronger interbank demand for term loans, dealers said.
They said banks sought 22 million kuna against supply of 40 million. But only 16.6 million were settled as borrowers and lenders could not agree on terms.
Call money and one-day bank rates were flat at 9.0 percent, with other loans higher at 11 to 21 percent, depending on term.
Insurers granted short-term funds at a steady 8.0 percent.
Thanks to very low shortfalls at commercial banks, Tuesday's overnight trade totalled only 5.9 million kuna.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Thursday were weaker at 5.4282 against the dollar and slightly firmer at 3.5677 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
